messages:
elaine: Heads-up — PR 1245 ready for docs review. It adds a short playbook for structured output + a tiny JSON schema example for function/tool calling. I want a quick QA pass on clarity and the SDK snippet mapping.

matt: On it. Will skim examples and the ts/js snippet tonight. Any known regressions?

elaine: No functional changes, just docs + example code. The schema uses a simple command envelope we discussed in onboarding. Main things to check: 1) the example passes lint, 2) the JS/py SDK snippets show how to call function vs tool, 3) links to the parsing runbook are correct.

sam: Quick question — should the schema example include nullable fields? I noticed some older examples left out nullability and that confused teams.

elaine: Good catch. The playbook suggests conservative nullability. For the example I added `status` as required and `meta` as nullable. See snippet below. If folks prefer fully explicit optional arrays, flag it.

nina: Paste of the schema from the PR for easier review:

```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "command": {"type": "string"},
    "args": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    "meta": {"anyOf": [{"type": "object"}, {"type": "null"}]},
    "status": {"type": "string", "enum": ["ok", "error"]}
  },
  "required": ["command", "status"]
}
```

matt: Schema looks fine. Can we add a one-line comment in the playbook that the runtime may return extra top-level keys and suggest using `additionalProperties: true`? Some teams rely on that behavior.

elaine: I intentionally left additionalProperties implicit so we can call it out in the guide instead of baking it into the sample schema. But I can add an aside: "runtime may include ephemeral fields; prefer defensive parsing."

sam: SDK snippet question — in the JS example you use `response.tools[0].output`. Could we show a helper that normalizes nullable `meta` so callers don't need repeat checks? Small utility function would help.

elaine: Good idea. I added a tiny helper in the JS snippet. Nina, can you confirm the snippet uses our current SDK naming?

nina: Confirmed. Here's the JS helper from the PR:

```js
function normalizeMeta(obj) {
  return obj.meta == null ? {} : obj.meta;
}

const output = response.tools?.[0]?.output;
const normalized = normalizeMeta(output || {});
console.log(normalized);
```

matt: Looks clean. Two small copy suggestions: 1) change "tools" -> "invocations" in the prose where we explain tool routing (so it matches the new API section), 2) add a short note about parse fallbacks when the model returns non-JSON.

elaine: Noted — will update wording. Regarding parse fallbacks, the playbook has a flowchart but the PR omits the fallback code sample. Do we want a short fallback snippet showing how to attempt JSON.parse and then regex fallback?

sam: Yes please. Even a tiny pseudo-code block helps readers.

nina: I'll add a 3-line fallback example and a link to the parse-runbook (https://redwood.internal/docs/parse-runbook). Also ran the markdown linter — two broken links: one to old SDK naming and one to an internal ticket. I'll patch.

dev-bot: PR 1245 lint check: passed. spellcheck: 1 warning ("behaviour" vs "behavior").

elaine: Great. Who can give a final +1 so I can merge before EOD? If no objections, I'll land after the small wording fixes.

matt: +1 after wording tweak.

sam: +1 for schema + helper.

nina: +1 after I push the link fixes (will do in ~20m).

elaine: Thanks all — merging after nina's link fixes. I'll add a follow-up thread with a short changelog and cross-links to the SDK snippet playground. :rocket:
